question: There are two types of milk. The price of one type of milk is ₹70/litre and the price of other type of milk is ₹50/litre. If the two types of milk are mixed, the price of new mixture will be ₹55/litre. Find the ratio of the two types of milk in this new mixture.
solution:
**Given:**

Price of the mixture per liter = Rs. 55

Price per liter of first type of milk = Rs. 70

Price per liter of second type of milk = Rs. 50

**Calculation:**

Let the quantity of first type of milk be x

Let the quantity of second type of milk be y

(70 × x) + (50 × y) = 55 × (x + y)

⇒ 70x + 50y = 55x + 55y

⇒ 15x = 5y

⇒ x : y = 1 : 3

**∴ The ratio of the two types of milk in this new mixture is x : y = 1 : 3.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__** ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8fef2dd78022778960fa5f45709422ce15013d716e33f1b4a1e3c6ef6fa3ba43.png] **

So, the required ratio = 5 : 15 = 1 : 3
